Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 50-y/o female with 5–6-day history of persistent dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias; impression most consistent with an acute viral upper respiratory tract infection.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Continuous dry, non-productive cough beginning 5–6 days ago; interferes with sleep.
- Associated symptoms: Runny nose, subjective chills/shivering (no temperature taken), generalized myalgias/weakness, transient diarrhea at onset (resolved). No dyspnea on usual activity, no chest pain, no sputum, no nausea/vomiting, appetite preserved, normal urination, no ear pain/discharge, no skin rash.
- Pertinent negatives: No significant sore-throat pain on swallowing, no wheeze, no hemoptysis.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin; Lisinopril.
- Allergies: Denies drug allergies.
- Family history: Father with type 2 diabetes.
- Social / preventive: Lives with partner (well); IT developer; former smoker (quit 6 mo ago); alcohol—wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week (advised reduction). Up-to-date routine care for diabetes/HTN per patient.

Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals recorded.
- No physical examination findings documented.

Impression:
- Most likely: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness (high likelihood given acute onset of cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, transient GI upset).
- Alternate considerations:
  • Early or viral bronchitis (medium likelihood; dry cough predominant but duration short).  
  • Atypical community-acquired pneumonia (low–medium; diabetes is a risk factor, but absence of dyspnea, focal chest signs makes less likely).

Plan:
- Symptomatic management: Rest, adequate hydration, regular paracetamol for comfort.
- Activity: Off work 1–2 days while symptoms acute; reassess before returning.
- Red-flag/worsening advice: Return sooner if breathing becomes labored, fever develops, or cough persists or worsens after 2–3 more days; may consider chest exam and antibiotics at that point.
- General health: Reduce alcohol intake (target ≤2 glasses/week initially) to support BP and diabetes control; continue smoking cessation.
- Routine care: Continue Metformin and Lisinopril; maintain usual diabetes/HTN follow-up.
- Follow-up: Re-contact clinic if no improvement within 2–3 days or any red-flag symptoms; otherwise expect resolution within ~7–10 days.

Quality checks
● Missing but expected: Temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO₂, lung auscultation; vaccination status (influenza/COVID); explicit follow-up date.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Moderate; teleconsultation without objective exam or vitals.
